story: In 1911 a former Louvre worker walked out with the Mona Lisa; it was missing two years, Picasso was questioned, and it was recovered in Florence in 1913.

es.caption:
Perdí a la Mona Lisa durante dos años. ¿Qué monumento debería contar su historia? 👇

En agosto de 1911, Vincenzo Peruggia, que había trabajado en el Louvre, sacó la Mona Lisa del museo vestido como empleado. La policía llegó a interrogar a Pablo Picasso, y la gente hacía visitas solo para ver la pared vacía. En 1913 intentó venderla en Florencia, el comerciante avisó a la policía y la pintura volvió a París.

Cada monumento tiene una historia así. Urban Tales te la cuenta mientras caminas. Link en la bio.

en.caption:
I lost the Mona Lisa for two years. Which landmark should tell its story next? 👇

In August 1911, Vincenzo Peruggia, who had worked at the Louvre, took the Mona Lisa out of the museum dressed like a member of staff. Police even questioned Pablo Picasso, and visitors came just to stare at the empty wall. In 1913 he tried to sell it to a dealer in Florence, who called the police, and the painting went back to Paris.
